title: Poisoning Self-Evolving Security Policies in LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.33385v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Self-evolving defenses improve LLM-agent security by learning reusable policies from observed attacks. However, we demonstrate that this learning process itself can become an attack surface. Using SED (Self-Evolving Defense) in the AgentDojo benchmark, we construct a single prompt-injection episode that causes the defense to learn an over-broad policy and subsequently refuse legitimate requests. Across 10 Nemotron runs, every poisoned run over-refuses at least one legitimate task, while unrelated-task performance remains unchanged and the original prompt-injection defense remains effective. The attack also transfers to gpt-oss-120b; however, its poisoning mechanism depends on a successful initial prompt injection and therefore fails to activate when the target agent resists the underlying injection. translated_title: 毒化大语言模型智能体中自我进化的安全策略
translated_abstract: 自我进化的防御机制通过从观察到的攻击中学习可复用的策略来提升LLM智能体的安全性。然而，我们证明这一学习过程本身也可能成为攻击面。我们在AgentDojo基准中使用SED（自我进化防御），构造了一个单一的提示注入情节，使防御机制学习到过于宽泛的策略，从而随后拒绝合法请求。在10次Nemotron运行中，每一次被毒化的运行都至少过度拒绝了一个合法任务，同时无关任务的性能保持不变，且原有的提示注入防御依然有效。该攻击还可以迁移到gpt-oss-120b；然而，其毒化机制依赖于成功的初始提示注入，因此当目标智能体能够抵抗底层注入时，攻击便无法激活。相比之下，针对SED的判断器、策略合成、检索和组织机制的完整性导向攻击在我们的评估中均告失败。
tldr: 该论文揭示了一种新型攻击面：攻击者仅需一次提示注入即可毒化LLM智能体的自我进化防御机制，诱使其学习到过于宽泛的策略，从而导致系统持续过度拒绝合法请求。
en_tdlr: The paper reveals a novel attack surface: a single prompt injection can poison the self-evolving defense of LLM agents, tricking it into learning over-broad policies that persistently over-refuse legitimate requests.
